Nova music festival massacre: On 7 October 2023, the al-Qassam Brigades, the military wing of the Palestinian nationalist Islamist political organization Hamas, initiated a sudden attack on Israel from the Gaza Strip.
Of Junker landowner stock, this 'Iron Chancellor' practiced Realpolitik and engineered the unification of Germany, becoming its first chancellor in 1871 — who is he?
Otto von Bismarck: Chancellor of Germany from 1871 to 1890.
Twice imprisoned during a 1920s satyagraha protest, this Indian activist quit the Congress party in 1925 and went on to found the movement behind modern Dravidian politics. Who is he?
Periyar: Indian social activist and politician (1879–1973)
A former Kopassus special-forces officer, he became Indonesia's oldest first-term president when he took office in 2024 — which leader?
Prabowo Subianto: President of Indonesia since 2024. In early 2008, Prabowo's inner circle established the Gerindra Party.
For three decades this Malagasy statesman served as prime minister and co-king of Madagascar, succeeding his own older brother in the role — who was he?
Rainilaiarivony: Prime Minister of Madagascar from 1864 to 1895.
Before circling the Moon 45 times as command module pilot on Apollo 12, this naval aviator had already flown in space piloting Gemini 11 — which astronaut?
Richard F. Gordon Jr.: American astronaut and lunar explorer (1929–2017)
Appointed Deputy to the Führer, this Nazi leader stunned everyone by flying solo to Scotland in 1941 to try to negotiate Britain out of the war — who was he?
In October 2025, she became the first woman ever to serve as Prime Minister of Japan — who is she?
Sanae Takaichi: Prime Minister of Japan since 2025. Takaichi's administration has consistently polled high in approval ratings.

Entering a power-sharing arrangement with his father in 2022, this politician became president after winning 73% of the vote in what's widely considered a sham election, making his nation the first in modern Central Asia ruled by a father-son dynasty — who is he?
Serdar Berdimuhamedow: President of Turkmenistan since 2022.

In 1793, Royalist rebels in this vital French naval port — home to a third of the French fleet — invited a 13,000-strong Anglo-Spanish force to help hold the city against advancing Republican troops — what military engagement was this?
Siege of Toulon (1793): Part of the War of the First Coalition.

This doctrine holding that governing authority is legitimate to some degree — especially over taxation and production — gained traction in American political discourse during the 1930s and '40s, its opposite being anarchism — what's it called?

Statism: Doctrine that the political authority of the state is legitimate to some degree. In political science, statism or etatism (from French, état 'state') is the doctrine that the political authority of the state is legitimate to some degree.
He led the first government of Bangladesh as prime minister during the 1971 War of Independence and is seen as one of the most instrumental figures in the nation's birth — who was he?
Tajuddin Ahmad: Prime Minister of Bangladesh from 1971 to 1972.
Chief minister who engineered Henry VIII's break from Rome to annul his marriage to Catherine of Aragon, this powerful statesman was beheaded in 1540 — a loss the king later regretted. Who was he?

Serving as the eighth U.S. director of national intelligence starting in 2025, this former Hawaii congresswoman deployed to Iraq with the National Guard and later left the Democrats to become a Republican — who is she?
Tulsi Gabbard: American politician and military officer (born 1981)

Set to become just the fourth queen to rule her Scandinavian kingdom in her own right — and the first since 1720 — she is heir apparent thanks to a 1980 law that was Western Europe's first with absolute primogeniture. Who is she?
Victoria, Crown Princess of Sweden: Heir apparent to the Swedish throne (born 1977)

In June 2014, forces captured the cities of Mosul and Tikrit, prompting Prime Minister Nouri al-Maliki to call for a national state of emergency that parliament refused to grant — which conflict was this?
War in Iraq (2013–2017): Armed Conflict in the Middle East.
A social worker shaped by the 1960s and the Occupation of Alcatraz, she became the first woman elected Principal Chief of the Cherokee Nation — who is she?
Wilma Mankiller: Cherokee Nation chief and activist (1945–2010)
Once called 'perhaps the most famous singer alive' in much of Africa, this Senegalese star helped develop the mbalax genre and even served as his country's Minister of Tourism — who is he?
Youssou N'Dour: Senegalese politician and musician (born 1959)
Who among these was born first?
Henry Vaughan (born 1621) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these people was born first?
Stephen Hales (born 1677) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these four was born earliest?
Qian Xuesen (born 1911) is the earliest of the four. Qian received his undergraduate education in mechanical engineering at National Chiao Tung University in Shanghai in 1934.
COBOL (founded 1959) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is an astronomer?
Who among these is a mathematician?
Leonhard Euler is a mathematician. Euler has been called a "universal genius" who "was fully equipped with almost unlimited powers of imagination, intellectual gifts and extraordinary memory".
Pick the chemist from these four.
Maud Menten is a chemist. Maud Leonora Menten (March 20, 1879 – July 17, 1960) was a Canadian physician and chemist.
What is the atomic number of Silicon?
Silicon (SILL-ih-kən) is a chemical element; it has symbol Si and atomic number 14.
In what year was Jerry Buss born?
Jerry Buss: Gerald Hatten Buss (January 27, 1933 – February 18, 2013) was an American businessman, investor, chemist, and philanthropist.
In what year was Pierre Curie born?
Pierre Curie (15 May 1859 – 19 April 1906) was a French physicist and chemist, and a pioneer in crystallography and magnetism.
In what year was Kevin Mitnick born?
Kevin Mitnick: Kevin David Mitnick (August 6, 1963 – July 16, 2023) was an American computer security consultant, author, and convicted hacker.
In what year did John von Neumann die?
John von Neumann: During World War II, von Neumann worked on the Manhattan Project.
In what year did C. V. Raman die?
C. V. Raman: This phenomenon, a hitherto unknown type of scattering of light they called modified scattering, was subsequently termed the Raman effect or Raman scattering.
In what year was Euler's formula discovered?
Euler's formula: The formula is still valid if x is a complex number, and is also called Euler's formula in this more general case.
COBOL: CODASYL. COBOL (Common Business-Oriented Language;) is a compiled English-like computer programming language designed for business use.
Propofol: Pfizer. Propofol is the active component of an intravenous anesthetic used for induction and maintenance of general anesthesia.
Boxer (dog breed): German Empire. The Boxer is a medium to large, short-haired dog breed of mastiff-type, developed in Germany.
Who is credited with discovering Special relativity?
Special relativity: Albert Einstein. In physics, the special theory of relativity, or simply special relativity, is a scientific theory of the relationship between space and time.
Who is credited with discovering Carbon dioxide?
Carbon dioxide: Jan Baptist van Helmont. Carbon dioxide is a chemical compound with the chemical formula CO2.
Who is credited with discovering Calcium?
Calcium: Humphry Davy. Calcium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ca and atomic number 20.
Made of adenine bonded to a sugar, this RNA building block underlies ATP, the cell's main energy currency, and doubles as an IV treatment for certain cardiac arrhythmias — what is it?
Adenosine (symbol A) is an organic compound that occurs widely in nature in the form of diverse derivatives.
The simplest pnictogen hydride, with the formula NH3, this pungent gas is also a common nitrogenous waste in living things — what is it?
Ammonia is an inorganic chemical compound of nitrogen and hydrogen with the formula NH3.
Sharing the 1974 Nobel Prize in Physics with Martin Ryle for the discovery of pulsars, which British radio astronomer had already earned the Royal Astronomical Society's Eddington Medal in 1969?

Antony Hewish (11 May 1924 - 13 September 2021) was a British radio astronomer who won the Nobel Prize for Physics in 1974 (together with fellow radio-astronomer Martin Ryle) for his role in the discovery of pulsars.
Which genus of early hominins, which lived in Africa during the Pliocene and Early Pleistocene, gave rise to the genera Homo, Paranthropus, and Kenyanthropus?
Australopithecus (-loh-; or, os-, from Latin australis southern 'grc' and (pthkos) ape) is a genus of early hominins that existed in Africa during the Pliocene and Early Pleistocene.
Often called a 'chest cold,' this inflammation of the airways in the lungs typically follows an infection that spreads down from the nose or throat. What condition is it?
Biceps is a large muscle that lies on the front of the upper arm between the shoulder and the elbow.

Derived from Greek words for 'slow' and 'heart', this medical term describes a resting heart rate under 60 beats per minute — sometimes a red flag, sometimes just a sign of a well-conditioned athlete. Name the condition?
Bradycardia (brads), meaning "slow", and (karda), meaning "heart", also called bradyarrhythmia, is a resting heart rate under 60 beats per minute (BPM).
This opportunistic yeast lives harmlessly in the gut and mouth of most healthy adults, but can turn pathogenic in immunocompromised people, causing a common fungal infection — what species is it?
Candida albicans is an opportunistic pathogenic yeast that is a common member of the human gut flora.
In calculus, this formula lets you find the derivative of a composed function h(x) = z(y(x)) using the derivatives of z and y separately — what is it called?
Chain rule is a formula that expresses the derivative of the composition of two differentiable functions z and y in terms of the derivatives of z and y.

From a tree in the myrtle family, these dried flower buds from the Moluccas are harvested year-round across different countries and lend their scent to everything from cosmetics to cooking — what are they?
Clove are the aromatic flower buds of a tree in the family Myrtaceae, Syzygium aromaticum.
Released on a daily cycle and spiking when you're stressed, this glucocorticoid raises blood sugar through gluconeogenesis and even tamps down the immune system — what stress hormone is it?
Cortisol is a steroid hormone in the glucocorticoid class of hormones and a stress hormone.
This progressive, incurable neurocognitive syndrome — often tied to Alzheimer's — brings a decline in memory, thinking and motivation across mild-to-major stages. What is it?

Dementia is a syndrome, often associated with neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's, and characterized by a general decline in cognitive processes that affects the ability to perform everyday activities.

Defined in humans as an adult height of 147 centimeters or less, this condition can be disproportionate (affecting limbs or torso alone) or proportionate, and typically comes with normal intelligence and near-normal life expectancy — which condition?
Dwarfism is a condition of people and animals marked by unusually small size or short stature.

This broad set of measures — taken by individuals, advocacy groups, and governments alike — aims to prevent pollution, conserve natural resources, and maintain ecological balance, sometimes repairing existing damage — what is it called?
Environmental protection refers to the taking of measures to protecting the natural environment, prevent pollution and maintain ecological balance.
Native to Mediterranean shores, this hardy perennial herb tastes much like anise and lends its flavor to absinthe; one variety swells into a bulb you can eat as a vegetable — what is it?
Fennel (Foeniculum vulgare) is a flowering plant species in the carrot family.
This American video game businessman dropped out of Harvard to join Microsoft, where he worked on early Windows and a Doom port, before co-founding Valve Corporation in 1996 — who is he?
Gabe Newell (born November 3, 1962), also known by his nickname GabeN, is an American video game developer and businessman.
One of Europe's smallest songbirds, this kinglet sports a bright orange-and-yellow crest in males and closely resembles the firecrest — which bird?
Goldcrest (Regulus regulus) is a very small passerine bird in the kinglet family.

A spiny mammal with 17 species across five genera in Europe, Asia, and Africa, this creature shares distant ancestry with shrews. There are no native populations in Australia or the Americas, though one extinct genus once roamed North America—what is it?
Hedgehog is a spiny mammal of the subfamily Erinaceinae, in the eulipotyphlan family Erinaceidae.
A colourless, ammonia-scented liquid with formula N2H4, this hazardous compound foams polymers, inflates airbags, and serves as a storable spacecraft propellant. What is it?
Hydrazine is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula N2H4.
Lasting anywhere from a few days to over a month, this disorder makes it hard to fall or stay asleep, leaving daytime drowsiness, irritability and trouble focusing in its wake — what is it?
Insomnia is a sleep disorder causing difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep for as long as desired.
Best known for his laws of planetary motion, this German astronomer has also been called the 'father of science fiction' for his novel Somnium. Who is he?
Johannes Kepler (27 December 1571 - 15 November 1630) was a German polymath who was an astronomer, mathematician, astrologer, natural philosopher and music theorist.
About the size of a domestic chicken, these flightless New Zealand natives turn out to be more closely related to Madagascar's extinct elephant birds than to the giant moa — what are they?
Kiwi (bird) are flightless birds endemic to New Zealand of the order Apterygiformes.
This Chinese herbalist, martial artist, and tactical advisor died in 1933 claiming a birth year of 1677 — a longevity claim gerontologists now regard as myth — who was he?
Li Ching-Yuen (simplified; traditional; pinyin: L Qngyn, died 6 May 1933) was a Chinese herbalist, martial artist and tactical advisor, known for his supposed extreme longevity.
Caused by a compromised lymphatic system, this condition raises infection risk in affected tissue and is treated with compression and massage rather than water pills — what is it?
Lymphedema (USA), lymphoedema (UK) also known as lymphatic edema (US)/oedema (UK), is a condition of localized swelling caused by a compromised lymphatic system.
This genus of flowering plants belongs to the chamomile tribe of the sunflower family, and several of its species go by the folk name 'mayweed' — which genus?
Matricaria is a genus of flowering plants in the chamomile tribe within the sunflower family.
First flown by the Soviet Air Force in 1968 and still in Russian production today, this medium chopper carries the NATO reporting name 'Hip' — what aircraft is it?
Mil Mi-8 is a family of medium twin-turbine helicopters, originally designed by the Soviet Central Aerohydrodynamic Institute (TsAGI) in the 1960s and introduced into the Soviet Air Force in 1968.

Caused when fly larvae burrow into and feed on an animal's tissue, this parasitic infestation is triggered by open wounds but can occur on unbroken skin when species such as the botfly are involved — name this condition?
Myiasis (my-), also known as flystrike or fly strike, is the parasitic infestation of the body of a live animal by fly larvae (maggots) that grow inside the host while feeding on its tissue.

Jointly operated by the U.S. Air Force and NASA in the 1960s, this rocket-powered experimental aircraft set speed and altitude records, once reaching Mach 6.7 and crossing into the edge of outer space — name this aircraft?

North American X-15 is a hypersonic rocket-powered aircraft formerly operated by the United States Air Force and the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) as part of the X-plane series of experimental aircraft.
Triggered by a surge of luteinizing hormone near the midpoint of the cycle, this event sees an ovarian follicle rupture and release an egg ready to be fertilized. What's the term?
Ovulation is an important part of the menstrual cycle in female vertebrates where the egg cells are released from the ovaries as part of the ovarian cycle.

This short-acting barbiturate is used as a sedative and anticonvulsant in low doses, but in high doses causes fatal respiratory arrest, making it a drug of choice for both veterinary euthanasia and U.S. executions — what is it?
Pentobarbital (US) or pentobarbitone (British and Australian) is a short-acting barbiturate typically used as a sedative, a preanesthetic, and to control convulsions in emergencies.
Equal to one-eighth of a gallon in both the imperial and US customary systems, this unit of volume is just over 20% larger in Britain than it is in America — name it?
Pint (symbol pt, sometimes abbreviated as p) is a unit of volume or capacity in both the imperial and United States customary measurement systems.

This corticosteroid drug treats a huge range of conditions — from rheumatoid arthritis and asthma to eye inflammation and certain cancers — and can be taken orally, injected, or applied to the skin. What is it?
Prednisolone is a corticosteroid, a steroid hormone used to treat certain types of allergies, inflammatory conditions, autoimmune disorders, and cancers, electrolyte imbalances, and skin conditions.
A zoonotic virus that triggers violent movements, a dread of water, and almost certain death once symptoms set in — usually one to three months after exposure. What is this disease?
Rabies is a zoonotic viral disease that causes acute and severe encephalitis in humans and other mammals.
Made by steaming dehusked oat groats before flattening them under heavy rollers and lightly toasting them, this whole-grain food becomes porridge when cooked — which product?
Rolled oats are a type of lightly processed whole-grain food.
Before becoming a full-time cartoonist in 1995, this creator of a hit workplace-satire comic strip worked various corporate jobs — who is he?
Scott Adams (June 8, 1957 - January 13, 2026) was an American cartoonist, author, and commentator.
Typically a bony enclosure around a vertebrate's brain, though cartilage in some fish and amphibians, this head structure combines a neurocranium with a facial skeleton — name it?

Skull is typically a bony enclosure around the brain of a vertebrate. In a human, the skull comprises two prominent parts: the neurocranium and the facial skeleton, which evolved from the first pharyngeal arch.
Named from the Greek word for tallow, this soft waxy 18-carbon saturated fatty compound is common in animal fats like beef tallow and lard — what is it called?
Stearic acid (stee-) is a saturated fatty acid with an 18-carbon chain.

Named after a figure from Greek mythology condemned to eternal frustration, this hard, corrosion-resistant blue-gray metal, atomic number 73, is mined alongside the chemically similar niobium in the ore known as coltan. What element is this?
Tantalum is a chemical element; it has symbol Ta and atomic number 73.
The largest member of the genus Panthera and an apex predator of Asian forests, this big cat wears orange fur striped in mostly-vertical black — what is it?
Tiger (Panthera tigris) is a large cat and a member of the genus Panthera native to Asia.
This broad category of large, hoofed mammals was reclassified in 2001 into a new clade after genetic data revealed the older grouping wasn't a true evolutionary lineage. Name the category of animals?
Ungulate are members of the diverse clade Euungulata, which primarily consists of large mammals with hooves.
This unit of time, equal to seven days, serves as the standard calendrical period between a day and a month in most of the world. What is it?
Week (in the Western and international context) is a unit of time equal to seven days.
First synthesized by chemist Alexander Shulgin in 1974, this psychedelic compound produces hallucinogenic effects considered milder than LSD or psilocybin — what is it commonly known as?
2C-B: Psychedelic drug. 2C-B, also known as 4-bromo-2,5-dimethoxyphenethylamine or by names such as Nexus or Erox, is a psychedelic drug of the phenethylamine and 2C families.
Also known as the buckeye or conker tree, this deciduous flowering tree is often confused with the unrelated sweet chestnut — which species?
Aesculus hippocastanum: Species of tree in the soapberry family.
Named for its carbon-carbon double bond, this class of hydrocarbon includes terminal versions known as alpha-olefins — what's the general term for it?
Alkene: Hydrocarbon compound containing one or more C=C bonds.
This group of diseases occurs when misfolded proteins accumulate in body tissue, causing fatigue, swelling, and shortness of breath among roughly 36 distinct protein-driven types — what is it?
Amyloidosis: Metabolic disease involving abnormal deposited amyloid proteins.
Unlike fear, which responds to a threat that's already here, this emotional state involves dread over something that hasn't happened yet, often paired with pacing and rumination. What is it?
Ranking as the second-largest lizard species after the Komodo dragon, this excellent swimmer thrives in lakes, rivers, and even city sewers across South and Southeast Asia — what is it?
Asian water monitor: Species of lizard. The Asian water monitor (Varanus salvator) is a large varanid lizard native to South and Southeast Asia.
As the largest member of the grass family, one species of this plant can grow stalks over 46 meters tall and 36 centimeters thick — name the plant?
Bamboo: Subfamily of plants in the grass family.
According to scholar John Carter, this discipline has two senses: a list of works consulted by an author, and the systematic study of books as physical objects — what's it called?
Bibliography: Organized listing of books and the systematic description of them as objects.
Built to replace the AH-1 Cobra, this twin-turboshaft attack helicopter packs a nose-mounted 30 mm chain gun and Hellfire missiles, with a two-person tandem cockpit — which aircraft is it?

Boeing AH-64 Apache: U.S. attack helicopter. The Apache began as the Model 77 developed by Hughes Helicopters for the United States Army's Advanced Attack Helicopter program to replace the AH-1 Cobra.

Native to Europe, West Asia, and parts of North Africa, this widely introduced game fish is one of the world's worst invasive species outside its home range, with regional names like sewin in Wales and finnock in Scotland — which species is it?
Brown trout: Species of fish. Brown trout are highly adaptable and have evolved numerous ecotypes/subspecies.

Derived from an East Asian evergreen tree's wood, this waxy, strong-smelling terpenoid can also be synthesized from oil of turpentine and occurs in small amounts in rosemary leaves. What compound is it?
An obligate carnivore with retractable claws and crepuscular hunting habits, this small domesticated mammal communicates with everything from purrs and trills to hisses — what is it?
Cat: Small domesticated carnivorous mammal. The cat (Felis catus), also called domestic cat and house cat, is a small domesticated carnivorous mammal.
Nicknamed 'Vigorous Dragon' and known to NATO as the Firebird, this Chinese delta-wing, canard-design fighter jet has been exported to Pakistan's air force — which aircraft, capable of Mach 1.8?
Chengdu J-10: Chinese multi-role fighter aircraft family.
Named after the French missionary who propagated it in Algeria, this citrus hybrid of mandarin and sweet orange is often sold as an 'Easy-peeler' — which fruit?
Clementine: Hybrid citrus fruit. The exterior is a deep orange colour with a smooth, glossy appearance.

Nocturnal and marked with narrow white crossbands on a bluish-black body, this South Asian snake's potent neurotoxic venom places it among the region's 'Big Four' most dangerous species — which snake?
Common krait: Species of snake. The common krait (Bungarus caeruleus) is a highly venomous snake species belonging to the genus Bungarus in the family Elapidae.
Nicknamed the mosquito hawk, which long-legged insect of the superfamily Tipuloidea is often mistaken for an oversized mosquito?
Crane fly: Superfamily of flies. The larvae of crane flies are known commonly as leatherjackets.
First created in 1994 and named for the German city where it was made, this synthetic element sits below platinum in group 10 — what is it?
Darmstadtium: Chemical element with atomic number 110 (Ds)
Produced by the enzyme 5α-reductase acting on a more familiar male sex hormone, this compound is a more potent driver of prostate growth, sebum, and body hair — which hormone?
Sometimes called 'word blindness,' this learning disability makes it hard to spell, sound out words, and read quickly, and often co-occurs with ADHD — what is it?

Often tangled up with mood, temperament, and creativity, these neurophysiological states carry a degree of pleasure or displeasure — yet scientists still can't agree on a single definition. What are they?
Dubbed the 'father of geometry,' this ancient Greek mathematician's treatise Elements dominated the field for nearly two thousand years — who is he?
This membranous bodily structure comes in superficial, visceral, and deep types, and a dangerous pressure buildup within it can cause compartment syndrome — what is it called?
Fascia: Layer of connective tissue in the body.
Sold under the brand name Prozac, this SSRI treats depression, OCD and panic disorder, and is also prescribed off-label for premature ejaculation — what is it?
Fluoxetine: SSRI antidepressant. It is also approved for treatment of major depressive disorder in adolescents and children 8 years of age and over.
Tucked beneath the liver, this pear-shaped organ stores and concentrates bile before releasing it to aid fat digestion in the small intestine — which organ?
Gallbladder: Organ in humans and other vertebrates.
The last survivor of an order that first appeared over 290 million years ago, this long-lived East Asian tree with unique fan-shaped leaves is celebrated as a living fossil — what is it?
Ginkgo biloba: Species of tree. Fossils similar to the living species, belonging to the genus Ginkgo, extend back to the Middle Jurassic epoch about 170 million years ago.

After proving a 20-year-old open problem in Riemannian geometry known as the soul conjecture, this reclusive Russian mathematician later quit the field entirely and now lives in seclusion in Saint Petersburg — who is he?
Grown as deciduous shrubs across the temperate Northern Hemisphere and related to the birch family, this plant produces a popular round brown nut — which plant genus?
Discovered in 1910 and stored in mast cells and basophils, this compound triggers immune responses and doubles as a neurotransmitter in the brain, spinal cord, and uterus — what is it?
Histamine: Organic compound involved in immune responses.
Teaching philosophy and astronomy in Roman-era Alexandria, this Neoplatonist is considered the first female mathematician whose life is well documented — who is she?
Sitting on the electromagnetic spectrum between visible light and microwaves, this invisible radiation makes up most of the black-body glow given off by objects near room temperature — what is it?

Infrared: Form of electromagnetic radiation. Infrared (IR; sometimes called infrared light) is electromagnetic radiation (EMR) with wavelengths longer than that of visible light but shorter than microwaves.
Working under Tamerlane around 1400, this Persian astronomer and mathematician produced work that mostly never reached Europe and stays largely unpublished — who is it?
Jamshid al-Kashi: Persian astronomer and mathematician (c. 1380–1429)
Before flying on Space Shuttle mission STS-128 in 2009, this Mexican-American engineer helped develop digital mammography equipment at Lawrence Livermore — who is he?
José M. Hernández: American engineer, vintner, and former NASA astronaut.
Also called German turnip despite not being related to true turnips, this stout cabbage cultivar can be eaten raw or cooked, stem and leaves alike — what vegetable?
Kohlrabi: Biennial cultivar of wild cabbage.
Called a 'universal genius,' this Swiss polymath founded graph theory and topology while introducing much of modern mathematical notation — who is he?
The third wide-body airliner to enter service after the 747 and DC-10, this trijet used an S-duct to route its third engine through the tail — which aircraft?

Lockheed L-1011 TriStar: American wide-body trijet airliner. The Lockheed L-1011 TriStar (pronounced "El-ten-eleven") is an American medium-to-long-range, wide-body trijet airliner built by the Lockheed Corporation.
A chemical engineer and physician who also served in the Peace Corps, she became the first African-American woman in space aboard Endeavour in 1992 — who is she?
Mae Jemison: American astronaut, doctor and engineer (born 1956)
Growing out of calculus and the study of derivatives and integrals, this branch of mathematics examines functions, spaces, and limits using methods of approximation and convergence — which field?

Mathematical analysis: Branch of mathematics. Mathematical analysis is the branch of mathematics that studies functions, spaces, and operators through quantitative methods of approximation and convergence.
This scientific field studies the atmosphere and short-term weather phenomena, with applications spanning aviation, agriculture, and disaster management — what field is it?
Meteorology: Scientific study of the atmosphere focusing on weather forecasting.
Cultivated by the Aztecs and named partly for a Mexican state capital, this flower opens each evening between four and eight o'clock and perfumes the night before closing by morning — which plant?

Mirabilis jalapa: Species of flower. Mirabilis jalapa, the marvel of Peru or four o'clock flower, is the most commonly grown ornamental species of Mirabilis plant, and is available in a range of colors.
Sold under the brand name Bactroban, this topical antibiotic treats impetigo and clears MRSA from the nose — what is it?
This general term describes inflammation of the kidneys, affecting structures such as the glomeruli, tubules, or the surrounding interstitial tissue — what is the condition called?
Nephritis: Inflammation of the kidneys. It is one of several different types of nephropathy.
This Turkish-born American economist, a Harvard-trained NYU professor, earned lasting fame as one of the few who foresaw the 2008 subprime mortgage crisis. Who is he?
Common in adolescents during growth spurts, this condition causes a painful bump just below the knee from inflammation where the patellar ligament attaches to the shinbone — what is it?

Osgood–Schlatter disease: Inflammation of the patellar ligament. Osgood–Schlatter disease (OSD) is inflammation of the patellar ligament at the tibial tuberosity (apophysitis) usually affecting adolescents during growth spurts.
This cream-skinned root vegetable, a cousin of the carrot and parsley, actually grows sweeter in flavor after a winter frost — what is it?
Parsnip: Root vegetable in the flowering plant family Apiaceae.
Secreted by eccrine and apocrine glands, this bodily fluid can flow at up to 4 litres per hour in adults and cools the body via evaporation — what is it?
Perspiration: Fluid secreted from sudoriferous glands.
Linked to prolonged sitting and excess hair, which skin condition causes a cyst to form between the cheeks of the buttocks and is treated with incision and drainage?
Pilonidal disease: Skin infection between the buttocks. Pilonidal disease is a type of skin infection that typically occurs as a cyst between the cheeks of the buttocks and often at the upper end.
Soft enough to slice with a knife, this silvery alkali metal carries the symbol K and takes its name from potash, the plant ashes it was first isolated from — what element is it?
Potassium: Chemical element with atomic number 19 (K)
This emotional response to severe distressing events like violence or a life-threatening injury can trigger flashbacks, panic attacks, insomnia, and post-traumatic stress disorder — what's it called?
Psychological trauma: Emotional response caused by severe distressing events.
This genus of roughly 1,750 flowering plant species includes the buttercups, spearworts, and water crowfoots — which genus?
Ranunculus: Genus of flowering plants in the buttercup family.
Extracted from the seeds of the castor oil plant, this lectin toxin carries an estimated lethal oral dose in humans of about one milligram per kilogram — what is it?
Also called false saffron, this thistle-like annual is one of the world's oldest crops, prized today for the vegetable oil pressed from its seeds — what plant is it?
Safflower: Species of plant. Safflower (Carthamus tinctorius), also false saffron, is a highly branched, herbaceous, thistle-like annual plant in the family Asteraceae.
This synthetic element, number 106, holds the rare distinction of being named after a scientist who was still alive at the time — its most stable isotopes survive mere minutes. What is it?
Seaborgium: Chemical element with atomic number 106 (Sg)

This primate group includes every animal traditionally called a monkey or ape — including humans — and split from the tarsiers roughly 60 million years ago. What's the term for this broader classification?
Also called dinkel wheat, this high-protein relict crop has been a staple in parts of Europe since the Bronze Age and is considered a hexaploid hybrid of common wheat and emmer — what is it?
Spelt: Species of wheat. It is a relict crop, eaten in Central Europe and northern Spain.

Headquartered in Kolkata, this Indian conglomerate spans FMCG, agribusiness, paper and packaging, yet still draws most of its revenue from tobacco — which company?
ITC Limited: Indian conglomerate. It has a presence across six business segments, namely FMCG, agribusiness, information technology, paper products, and packaging.
Founded in 1926 and based in Stuttgart, this German brand makes luxury cars and once handled heavy trucks before spinning them off to Daimler Truck — what is it?
Mercedes-Benz: German luxury automotive brand. Mercedes-Benz AG (a subsidiary of the Mercedes-Benz Group, established in 2019) is based in Stuttgart, Baden-Württemberg, Germany.
Along with his brothers, this physician-businessman acquired the pharmaceutical company that developed OxyContin, later linked to the U.S. opioid crisis — who is he?
Raymond Sackler: American physician and businessman (1920–2017)
Headquartered in Bengaluru, this food-delivery company operates in over 700 Indian cities and runs a quick-commerce arm called Instamart — which company?
Swiggy: Indian online food delivery company.
